description: Read, create, update and delete Outlook calendar events via Microsoft Graph, and find free time: list agendas, fetch event details, make scheduling changes, and search for open slots of a given length across calendars.

inputs.description: Where the API is; it must be allowed below
inputs.name: api_base
inputs.title: API base URL

instructions: Find events with listEvents before updating or deleting them; event IDs come from there. listEvents has no text search: Microsoft Graph documents $search only for messages, people and directory objects, not events, so narrow the time window instead. Times are RFC 3339 with offsets. Graph stores start/end as wall time plus a named timeZone, so always pass timeZone (a Windows or IANA name, e.g. "Pacific Standard Time" or "America/Los_Angeles") on create and findFreeTime, and on update when start or end change. "primary" is the user's default calendar. Use findFreeTime to propose open slots of a given length instead of scanning agendas by hand.
name: outlook-calendar
title: Outlook Calendar

tools.description: List events in a calendar: occurrences within a time window (recurring events expanded), or the most recent events when no window is given. Give both timeMin and timeMax, or neither.

calendarId.description: Calendar ID, or "primary" for the default calendar

timeMin.description: Start of the window, RFC3339, e.g. 2026-10-11T00:00:00-07:00

timeZone.description: Render start/end in this time zone (Windows or IANA name); defaults to UTC

tools.name: listEvents
tools.title: List events

tools.description: Get one event's full details: times, attendees, location, plain-text description

calendarId.description: Calendar ID, or "primary" for the default calendar

timeZone.description: Render start/end in this time zone (Windows or IANA name); defaults to UTC

tools.name: getEvent
tools.title: Get an event

tools.description: Create an event: subject, start and end (RFC3339 with offset) in the given timeZone, optional location, plain-text description, attendees, all-day flag

calendarId.description: Calendar ID, or "primary" for the default calendar

end.description: End, RFC3339, e.g. 2026-10-12T15:00:00-07:00 (a date for all-day events, exclusive)

isAllDay.description: True for an all-day event; start/end are then dates (YYYY-MM-DD)

start.description: Start, RFC3339, e.g. 2026-10-12T14:00:00-07:00 (a date for all-day events)

timeZone.description: Time zone for start/end: a Windows or IANA name, e.g. "Pacific Standard Time" or "America/Los_Angeles"

tools.name: createEvent
tools.title: Create an event

tools.description: Update an event; only the given fields change (patch semantics). timeZone is required when start or end change.

calendarId.description: Calendar ID, or "primary" for the default calendar

end.description: End, RFC3339 (a date for all-day events, exclusive)

isAllDay.description: True for an all-day event; start/end are then dates (YYYY-MM-DD)

start.description: Start, RFC3339 (a date for all-day events)

timeZone.description: Time zone for a changed start/end: a Windows or IANA name

tools.name: updateEvent
tools.title: Update an event

tools.description: Delete an event from the calendar

calendarId.description: Calendar ID, or "primary" for the default calendar

tools.name: deleteEvent
tools.title: Delete an event

tools.description: Find free time slots of at least a given length within a time window, across one or more calendars. One call asks the API for each calendar's agenda and computes the open slots, so the agent never does interval math by hand

calendarIds.description: Calendar IDs to consider; defaults to ["primary"]

durationMinutes.description: Minimum slot length in minutes (at least 5)

timeMin.description: Start of the window, RFC3339, e.g. 2026-10-11T00:00:00-07:00

timeZone.description: Time zone the agenda is read in: a Windows or IANA name, e.g. "Pacific Standard Time" or "America/Los_Angeles"

tools.title: Find free time
